findings.claim: Active domain questions name an owner and deferred stage but no deadline; Q-03 blocks the launch inventory scope and Q-09 blocks the refund policy.

findings.claim: Payment-failed re-purchase handling conflicts with cardinality: a new record is minted despite the single-entitlement rule and the stated reactivation rule.

evidence.excerpt: One entitlement per product per holder, always.
Terminal - a new purchase mints a new record.
An eligible re-purchase reactivates the existing record rather than minting a second.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose whether a retry or re-purchase reactivates the failed row or creates a second entitlement with its own seats and terms.
findings.failureScenario: The buyer receives duplicate rights, seat pools, or term lineages in the purchased library.

findings.claim: Library behavior preserves multiple rows for the same holder and product after distinct terms, gifts, or bundle overlap, without defining an exception to issuance singleton.

evidence.excerpt: One entitlement per product per holder, always.
Two rows. Never merged.
If one lands anyway (gift, bundle overlap), both rows persist.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the exception and mapping between issuance records and library rows, including terms and seat behavior.
findings.failureScenario: The library duplicates rights or exposes the wrong terms and seats for the same product.

findings.claim: The takedown rule stops onward delivery but does not define existing-holder archive access or one-asset versus whole-pack scope.

evidence.excerpt: Further delivery of the removed thing stops immediately; the holder's entitlement row persists.
Whether an existing holder may still fetch the archive is not stated.
The takedown granularity is also undefined.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose whether existing buyers can fetch removed builds and whether a takedown removes a single asset or an entire pack.
findings.failureScenario: The service either continues infringing delivery or removes promised bytes without a defined remedy.

findings.claim: Upgrade/base refunds are asserted as 'refund both or neither' and separately declared open.

evidence.excerpt: Refund both or neither.

findings.claim: Waiver cross-cuts use a two-limb, order-keyed, unconditional gate while the canonical feature requires three limbs, an entitlement key, and an expiry condition.

evidence.excerpt: The crosscut describes a two-limb waiver condition.
The waiver record is placed on the order.
No waiver, no transfer grant, no bytes.
The canonical gate requires all three limbs.
The canonical record is per entitlement, never order.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the waiver evidence key and the exact condition for granting digital access.
findings.failureScenario: Multi-item waivers are applied incorrectly, valid orders block re-downloads, or missing durable confirmation is accepted as a waiver.

findings.claim: Waiver behavior depends on trader status even though the vendor portal lacks the declaration and checkout lacks its required pre-buy disclosure.

evidence.excerpt: The gate branches on whether the seller is a trader.
The required record includes the seller's declared trader status.
14.08.01 has no such field today.
Trader-status disclosure must appear before the buy button.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose who declares and validates seller status, and which checkout gate selects the appropriate disclosure.
findings.failureScenario: Consumer-law disclosures are omitted for trader sales or incorrectly imposed on consumer-to-consumer sales.

findings.claim: An unresponsive split contributor freezes direct-sale payouts for everyone, but no timeout or fallback allocation exists.

evidence.excerpt: An unagreed split blocks payout, not publish.
Payout blocks when there is no answer.
Q-01 asks for a timeout or fallback for direct-sale proceeds.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose partial payout versus total hold and an allocation procedure after a contributor does not respond.
findings.failureScenario: Collected revenue remains indefinitely frozen or is distributed under an unapproved fallback.
